contribution.position: Holding my reliability position. Answering qa on axis:risk, whose claim is that cold_start is 600ms, comfortably inside the 800ms budget: that figure does not appear in artifact:perf-report, which records cold_start at 1900ms at peak load against the same 800ms budget. The 600ms number has no artifact behind it, so it cannot offset the overage. If it comes from a non-peak run, it measures a different condition than the one where the warmer matters. Qa should name the artifact and the load level, or retract the claim. New evidence since my last turn: the 3% cost in artifact:cost-sheet (product) and the v4 rollback steps in artifact:ops-runbook (ops) are real, but they bear on cost and recovery, not on whether cold_start at peak triggers a repeat of the retry storms behind the two sev2 incidents in artifact:incident-log. Nothing in the transcript or artifact list addresses retry or backoff behavior under peak load, and artifact:test-report (412 passed, 87% coverage) does not exercise it. The gap remains: a peak-load test showing cold_start within budget or a documented waiver, plus retry and backoff evidence under peak load.
